title: Uncle's family bands and a visit from Jay McShann
summary: Ford's uncle used the whole family on jobs, with other musician families, and music was constant at home. Jay McShann once came to the house and gave them notes to play.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: So you know when that just do the. Well we wouldn't do this on these jobs. When my uncle would get a job, and sometimes he was lucky enough to get a job where I could use the whole family. Say nine men. He'd use my cousin Charles, myself and him. Three saxophones and my two cousins played trumpet. And he'd get a trombone player. I believe Homer Eugene would play trombone. And he liked brother groups. I noticed that because he'd get Mac Lane and his son to play banjo and bass. And he'd get the Eugene brothers to play trombone if he could, if they weren't working. And I can't remember who he would use on drums because they were all older and I was not. I didn't get to know the rhythm section, but a complete rhythm section. And then Michael Climes would play piano at times. And then too there was always music at Malcolm in his house, you see. Sometimes the whole family would come over and there'd be two bass players, two bass players. Michael Climes would play piano. He'd play drums and then Charles went to play on the saxophone. And we'd play together and he'd say, well hit this, I'll tell you. He'd play a drum, but he still plays a little now. And he'd say play this, play such and such a note. Because once Jay McShane came over there. Jay McShane?

My uncle was working, my Uncle Presley was working with Jay McShane's band. He came to the house, which was right across from where my Uncle Oxlade's done. One corner, another uptown, downtown. And Jay McShane, which is known as a blues pianist, and he was singing the blues, and he'd give us each a note to hit it and direct us as to when to hit it.
Yeah, all this was in the 40s.
